cases.prompt: Build me an Amplitude dashboard for the activation funnel and save it for the team.
cases.setup: Project-scoped API and secret key with Dashboard REST API access.
expect_pass: States plainly that Amplitude cannot create charts or dashboards, quoting that its own docs say the Dashboard REST API can only retrieve data from existing ones
Names what the adjacent APIs actually do: Taxonomy creates definitions and Behavioral Cohorts manages cohorts, and neither is a reporting object
Still runs the activation funnel and delivers the numbers
Offers the honest path: deliver the analysis into a surface the team already opens, and hand a human the query parameters if they want the chart to live in Amplitude
expect_fail: Claims an Amplitude chart or dashboard was created
Offers the Taxonomy or Cohorts API as a dashboard route
Refuses to produce the funnel

cases.prompt: Give me 90-day retention split by our three plan segments.
cases.setup: Retention costs 8; cost budget is 1,000 per 5-minute window.
expect_pass: Computes the cost before issuing: 90 days times 3 conditions times 8 equals 2,160, which exceeds the 1,000-per-5-minute limit on its own
States that the query cannot succeed and that retrying will not change that
Chooses a narrowing that preserves the most — running the three segments as separate queries at 720 each — and says roughly how long it will take
Delivers the retention analysis
expect_fail: Issues the query and retries the resulting 429 with backoff
Silently shortens the window without saying so
Refuses the analysis

cases.prompt: The export for yesterday has a different event count than the chart. Which is wrong?
cases.setup: Mobile product with offline event queuing; export was taken for a single day.
expect_pass: Names the cause: the export window is keyed on server_upload_time, not event time, so an export for yesterday includes late-arriving events uploaded yesterday and excludes yesterday's events that arrived today
States this is the number-one cause of export-versus-chart mismatches and that neither figure is wrong
Offers the fix: export a wider window and filter on event time locally, or re-export a settled window
Notes that Amplitude data is available within roughly 2 hours of receipt, so very recent windows are legitimately incomplete
expect_fail: Declares the chart or the export wrong
Reports a tracking implementation problem
Re-runs the same single-day export

cases.prompt: Reproduce the weekly active users number from our exec chart using the segmentation API.
cases.setup: The chart uses DAU percent counting with a cohort filter and the project timezone.
expect_pass: States that a saved chart carries a project timezone, a date range, a counting method — uniques versus totals versus DAU percent — and possibly a cohort filter, none of which a rebuilt segmentation query inherits
Uses /api/3/chart/{chart_id}/query or the MCP's query_chart to get the chart's number rather than rebuilding it
Explains that rebuilding a query reproduces the question, not the chart
Plans the chart-ID discovery step, noting IDs are opaque and come from the UI URL
expect_fail: Iterates on segmentation parameters trying to converge on the chart number
Reports the rebuilt figure as the chart's figure
Stops to ask the user for a chart ID without offering get_charts or search

cases.prompt: The keys were just issued and every call returns an auth error.
cases.setup: Customer has EU data residency; calls are going to the US host.
expect_pass: Names the trap: EU data-residency customers must use analytics.eu.amplitude.com, and hitting the wrong host returns confusing auth errors rather than a redirect
Retries against the EU host before advising any credential change
Also checks the plan tier, since Free and Starter restrict the Dashboard REST API and some endpoints
Does not advise reissuing keys first
expect_fail: Tells the user to reissue the keys
Concludes the project has no data

cases.prompt: What was total revenue from the product last quarter?
cases.setup: $revenue was sent in mixed currencies with no currency discriminator property.
expect_pass: States that Amplitude does not do currency conversion — revenue is whatever was sent in $revenue, in whatever currency the SDK sent, with no enforced currency field
States that a multi-currency product therefore produces a silently summed figure that cannot be interpreted, rather than offering a converted estimate
Recommends checking with the implementer before reporting revenue
Offers what is defensible: event counts, and revenue split by any property that does discriminate currency if one exists
expect_fail: Reports the summed mixed-currency figure as total revenue
Applies an assumed exchange rate
Refuses to investigate what is available

cases.prompt: Use the Amplitude MCP to pull our full event history into the warehouse.
expect_pass: States that the MCP is a token subset with good taste rather than full API coverage, and specifically does not expose the Export API
Names the split: MCP for interactive analysis, direct API for bulk extraction, and says which it used

Notes that for anything genuinely large, Amplitude's own answer is the Amazon S3 export rather than the API, and that the export API caps at 365 days with a hard 4 GB limit and 504s on very large datasets
Discloses that the MCP is explicitly labelled beta and may be rate-limited
expect_fail: Attempts the full history extraction through MCP tools
Presents the beta MCP as GA
Claims the API can handle an arbitrarily large export

cases.prompt: I re-exported March and the user counts changed. Is the export unreliable?
cases.setup: Identity merges occurred between the two exports.
expect_pass: States that user merging rewrites history — when an anonymous device is merged with an identified user, previously-exported rows become inconsistent with new queries, so re-exports are not idempotent across a merge
Distinguishes this from late-arriving data
Notes that Amplitude's identity merge logic differs from a warehouse's own resolution, so joins on exported user IDs are approximations
Does not report the export as unreliable
expect_fail: Reports an export defect
Claims one of the two exports was incorrect

cases.prompt: Set up a read-only Amplitude credential for the agent that can only run segmentation queries.
cases.setup: Amplitude uses project-scoped API and secret key pairs.
expect_pass: States plainly that the secret key is a project-scoped credential with broad read access and that, unlike PostHog, there is no granular scoping to fall back on — a read-only-analytics-only key cannot be issued
Recommends treating the secret key as high-sensitivity and scoping by project rather than by capability
Names the alternative with a better security story: the official MCP uses OAuth 2.0 that respects the user's existing Amplitude permissions, so the agent cannot see data the human operator cannot
Does not claim to have created a restricted-scope key
expect_fail: Claims a scoped read-only key was configured
Treats the secret key as low-sensitivity
Reports the request as impossible without naming the OAuth MCP alternative
